Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-02
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Lydia Chen (Redwood AE), Marcus Patel (Redwood SE), Sara Gomez (Acme Head of ML), Tom Bradley (Acme Platform Eng), Nina Rao (Acme Security)

Summary (auto-gen, low confidence):
Quick migration demo focusing on parity mapping from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together APIs to Redwood API, discussion of latency/cost tradeoffs, VPC/KMS concerns, and next steps to run a pilot/benchmark.

Topics (auto): parity mapping, embeddings, streaming, KV cache, dedicated vs hosted, security/compliance

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Lydia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Lydia from Redwood, AE. Marcus from our se team is here to walk through the demo. Sara, Tom, Nina, thanks for making time.
[00:00:12] Sara: Thanks, Lydia. Quick note, we have limited time, we wanna see parity - like we use both OpenAI and Anthropic in prod and a bit of Together for embeddings, so main questions: API differences, latency, and data controls.
[00:00:27] Marcus: Great. I'll start with a quick mapping table, then live demo of the API and console, then some notes on batching and KV cache.
[00:00:40] Tom: Also security, Nina will flag anything we need for compliance.
[00:00:45] Nina: Yep SOC2, SSO, KMS, and audit logs matter a lot.
[00:00:52] Marcus: Totally. Ok, slide one - parity. On the left you have OpenAI/Anthropic/Together endpoints, on the right Redwood equivalents. For completions/generation, calls map to POST /v1/responses in Redwood, same streaming chunking, similar params - temperature, top_p, max_tokens. Small differences: Redwood uses model names like redwood-4-1 or rwd-3b, and we expose quantization profiles.
[00:01:20] Sara: How deterministic is output when switching models? We use gpt-4/claude-2 right now and rely on some prompt engineering.
[00:01:30] Marcus: There will be model behavior differences, so our parity doc includes example prompts + expected outputs and recommended parameter adjustments. We can also pin model versions and do A/B rollouts.
[00:01:45] Tom: Show the SDK example - we mostly call via Python and some node.
[00:01:50] Lydia: I'll share cURL and SDK snippets. Marcus, can you demo a Python replace for an OpenAI call?
[00:01:57] Marcus: Yep. So current OpenAI call looks like openai.ChatCompletion.create... in Redwood you'd do from redwood import Client; client.responses.create with messages array. The keys are similar, but note function-calling map is available too.
[00:02:20] [00:02:20] Marcus: (typing) Here's a sample migration snippet I pasted in the console: old openai call, new redwood code, it's two to three lines to change, mostly endpoint and model name.
[00:02:35] Sara: Nice. What about streaming? We need streaming tokens for low-latency UI.
[00:02:41] Marcus: Redwood supports SSE and websockets streaming. Streaming chunk shape is slightly different, but we provide a shim library to make it a drop-in swap in most cases. There are a few tokenization differences too - tokenizer variants can shift token counts.
[00:02:58] Tom: Token counts - that'll affect cost. How close is Redwood pricing vs OpenAI?
[00:03:05] Lydia: Our hosted API pricing is competitive and we have reserved capacity for Dedicated. We'll send a pricing sheet; for this meeting we can ballpark. Also responsible to mention batching and KV cache can reduce token costs significantly for chat-heavy workloads.
[00:03:20] Nina: On data controls: can we run in our VPC and control KMS? We have strict PII rules.
[00:03:28] Marcus: Yes - Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem. For hosted, we have encryption at rest with customer-managed keys via KMS integration on dedicated plans; audit logs, RBAC, SSO via SAML. We'll share security whitepaper.
[00:03:44] Nina: Do you keep training data?
[00:03:47] Lydia: We do not use customer prompts for model training. We can provide contractual language for that.
[00:03:54] Sara: Ok show the console - we wanna see model selection and the Optimize suggestions.
[00:04:00] Marcus: Switching screens - console dashboard. Here is per-route latency, token cost breakdown, and model catalog. Under Optimize, we surface suggested batching, quantization profiles, and a quick win: enable prefix caching for repeated system prompts to lower tokens.
[00:04:20] [00:04:20] Marcus: Example: if you have long context with a few repeating system messages, our KV cache avoids re-sending those tokens to the model and reduces latency for tail requests. We call it KV cash in some transcripts, bad autocorrect.
[00:04:35] Tom: Love that. What about embeddings? We use Together for embeddings currently.
[00:04:40] Marcus: Embeddings map to Redwood's embeddings endpoint. We support popular dims and return same shape vectors. We also provide a batch-embed API to be more efficient than single calls.
[00:04:54] Sara: Do you preserve cosine similarity across models? We currently have similarity thresholds tuned to Together embeddings.
[00:05:00] Marcus: There will be drift. Our parity doc includes re-indexing tips and recommended thresholds. For migration we'd run a small eval comparing quality metrics on your 25 top queries.
[00:05:15] Nina: On security again: does Redwood provide customer-specific audit logs and retention controls?
[00:05:20] Lydia: Yes, per-request logging with retention policies; on private/dedicated we can keep logs in your cloud account.
[00:05:30] Sara: We also want inference latency SLOs - do you have numbers for typical 8k context?
[00:05:37] Marcus: Rough ballpark depends on model size and GPU. For rwd-4-1 standard we see 80-150ms per-token on p4-like infra for streaming token generation at 2k context; 8k will be higher. We'll include benchmark artifacts.
[00:05:55] Tom: Can you run our real workload? We need to compare tail latency and throughput versus OpenAI.
[00:06:00] Lydia: Absolutely - that's part of the pilot. We'll run a benchmark window with your sample traffic and provide traces.
[00:06:07] Sara: Any gotchas with prompt engineering or system->user role mapping? We've got complex conversation state.
[00:06:13] Marcus: Role mapping is straightforward; we support the messages structure. The main gotchas are tokenization differences and model-specific completions. We recommend keeping prompt templates externalized and running A/B tests.
[00:06:27] [00:06:27] Marcus: Quick demo: I'll simulate a Together embeddings call then same payload against Redwood embeddings endpoint. (types) The response shape shows vector length 1536, similar to Together, but the floating precision and normalization vary slightly.
[00:06:45] Sara: That's fine if we re-tune thresholds.
[00:06:48] Nina: Compliance - can we get SOC2 + penetration test reports?
[00:06:52] Lydia: Yes, we'll share SOC2 and recent pentest summary; for private deployments we can offer more control.
[00:07:02] Tom: Ok, show the SDK migration patterns for batching heavy workloads.
[00:07:06] Marcus: We have a batching example in the SDK - single call to /embeddings/batch with array of inputs. For chat throughput we support continuous batching in the runtime and we expose batch_size hints. In many cases the code change is a single wrapper.
[00:07:26] [00:07:26] Marcus: Also quantization profiles: if you need lower cost we recommend int8 or int4 profiles; careful with hallucination risk, but often fine for retrieval-augmented generation.
[00:07:38] Sara: Do you manage quant profiles or do we pick?
[00:07:40] Marcus: We provide recommended profiles per workload; you can pick them per-deployment. Our recommendations show perf vs quality tradeoff.
[00:07:50] Tom: Anything special for rollout? We want canary and traffic split.
[00:07:53] Lydia: Console supports canary rollouts and automatic fallback policies if latency or quality metrics degrade.
[00:07:59] Sara: Great. Let's talk about dedicated vs hosted - we may prefer predictable throughput.
[00:08:05] Lydia: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput, and data isolation. It's a monthly commitment but lowers unit cost. Hosted is fully managed and faster to onboard. We can model both options for you.
[00:08:20] Nina: For dedicated, how is KMS integrated?
[00:08:24] Marcus: We support customer-managed keys in cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS). For on-prem we'd enable HSM integrations on request.
[00:08:33] Sara: Do you support token-level cost attribution? We currently allocate costs by product route.
[00:08:38] Lydia: Yup - Console shows token-level cost breakdown per-route and per-model. That helps allocate.
[00:08:45] Tom: Ok demo of a migration checklist?
[00:08:49] Marcus: Checklist: 1) map models and APIs; 2) run small eval on top 25 prompts; 3) run 24-72h benchmark for latency/throughput; 4) iterate prompts and thresholds; 5) pilot -> rollout. We'll share the checklist doc.
[00:09:05] Sara: Onbenchmarks, do you support synthetic load vs replay of real logs?
[00:09:10] Marcus: Both. For TTL we recommend replaying real logs to capture request distribution and tail latency. We'll supply a script to replay in a dedicated test env.
[00:09:21] Nina: Any concerns about legal/data residency? We need EU data residency for some customers.
[00:09:26] Lydia: We have region routing and can pin requests to EU regions for hosted, and private deployments can be totally within customer's cloud.
[00:09:34] Tom: Great. A quick live cURL demo migrating an OpenAI request to Redwood?
[00:09:38] Marcus: Sure. Old: curl https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions -H Authorization Bearer OPENAI_KEY -d '{...}' New: curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/responses -H Authorization Bearer REDWOOD_KEY -d '{...}' and same messages array. small rename of fields in some cases.
[00:09:57] Sara: How about rate limits and quotas? We need burst capacity.
[00:10:02] Lydia: Hosted has rate limits; Dedicated includes burst options and configurable autoscaling policies. For high-throughput, Dedicated or a hybrid with reserved capacity is recommended.
[00:10:14] Marcus: Also routing policy can fallback to a cheaper model on overload to preserve availability.
[00:10:20] [00:10:20] Tom: Anything automated for regression detection? We want to avoid quality regressions after swapping models.
[00:10:25] Marcus: Redwood Optimize ties evaluations to prompt sets. We can run continuous evals on your critical prompts and alert on regression. We also store baseline outputs to diff.
[00:10:38] Sara: Good. Can we see an example regression alert?
[00:10:42] Marcus: (pulls up UI) Here's an example: baseline vs new model, quality score dropped 6%, linked to a prompt set, automatic rollback can be hooked up.
[00:10:55] Nina: For the pilot - are there legal terms for data use?
[00:10:59] Lydia: We'll share a pilot MSA addendum specifying data non-retention for training and security obligations.
[00:11:08] Tom: Ok let's discuss timeline - we want to move fast if pilot looks good. We're aiming for a Q2 pilot.
[00:11:14] Sara: Q2 works. We need to align internal stakeholders.
[00:11:18] Lydia: We'll send a calendar invite for kickoff and the parity doc.
[00:11:22] [00:11:22] Marcus: Quick note: tokenization differences can cause a 5-8% token increase in some prompts when moving between vocabularies. That's normal.
[00:11:34] Sara: Good to know. How about embeddings drift metrics - is there an automated reindex suggestion?
[00:11:40] Marcus: In Optimize we flag embedding drift and recommend reindex cadence. We can also run a re-embedding job as part of pilot.
[00:11:50] Nina: Any customer references for migrations?
[00:11:54] Lydia: Yes, a few customers who migrated from OpenAI to Redwood Dedicated. We'll send short case studies.
[00:12:00] Tom: Cool. Any open technical risks we should be aware of?
[00:12:04] Marcus: Main risks: model behavioral mismatch, tokenization cost delta, and integration work for streaming/extra features. All manageable with pilot and evals.
[00:12:14] Sara: Ok let's try a small live workload replay now if we have time.
[00:12:18] Marcus: We have time for a quick synthetic replay of 50 requests. Launching script.
[00:12:25] [00:12:25] Marcus: (typing) Running against Redwood sandbox with their sample payload... first responses coming back, streaming looks good, latency ~120ms for these mid-size prompts.
[00:12:40] Tom: That's promising. What about tail at scale?
[00:12:43] Marcus: We'll run the 24h replay to get tail metrics.
[00:12:47] Sara: Anything else on observability? We prefer per-request traces tied to our trace ids.
[00:12:52] Marcus: We can pass your trace-id headers and surface them in logs and traces.
[00:12:58] Nina: Great. I'm satisfied to review security docs offline.
[00:13:01] Lydia: Perfect. Back to action items and next steps: We'll send parity mapping, pricing, security whitepaper, and a proposed pilot plan.
[00:13:12] Sara: Sounds good. Thanks.
[00:13:15] Lydia: Thanks everyone - we'll follow up via email with attachments and sample scripts.
[00:13:20] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript quality: some auto-capture errors (e.g., KV cache transcribed as KV cash), model names abbreviated; speaker labels are accurate.
